mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring any specific threshold condition.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS declines (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 10.0% for three consecutive months, it signals a severe labor market contraction that triggers aggressive monetary policy responses, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in 60% or more of instances where UNRATE > 10.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a dual stress on the housing market and labor market, which typically precedes a policy response that boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term between HOUST and UNRATE does not yield a positive Rank IC > 0.03 in any 2-year rolling window, or the 60-day returns are negative in 60% of instances where both conditions hold.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO below 90.0 index), the economy is in a supply shock contraction phase, which typically leads to a policy response that boosts equity markets, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in 60% or more of instances where INDPRO < 90.0.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth (GDPC1) over the past quarter indicates a strengthening economy, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days without requiring a specific threshold.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth does not correlate with positive 60-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals accelerating inflation that triggers a monetary tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in 60% or more of instances where CPIAUCSL 12m change > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a monetary policy response to a labor market downturn, which typically precedes a market rally, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term between FEDFUNDS and UNRATE does not yield a positive Rank IC > 0.03 in any 2-year rolling window, or the 20-day returns are negative in 60% of instances where both conditions hold.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high retail sales growth (RSAFS above 0.5% monthly), consumer spending is robust, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are supported.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in 60% or more of instances where RSAFS growth > 0.5% monthly.
